candidate.educational_objective: Respond to new tendon pain or swelling during ciprofloxacin therapy by stopping the drug, contacting the healthcare provider, and resting/refraining from exercise of the affected tendon.

options.A: Stop ciprofloxacin, contact the healthcare provider promptly, rest the affected tendon, and refrain from exercise until evaluated.
options.B: Continue ciprofloxacin while temporarily reducing running, and report the problem only if swelling or functional limitation worsens.
options.C: Continue ciprofloxacin and add a calcium supplement because calcium lowers the risk of fluoroquinolone tendon injury.
options.D: Finish the ciprofloxacin course before reporting tendon symptoms unless a tendon rupture occurs.

candidate.rationale: CIPRO carries a boxed warning for serious adverse reactions including tendinitis and tendon rupture. Current labeling directs immediate discontinuation if tendon pain, swelling, inflammation, or rupture occurs. Patient counseling specifically instructs patients with tendon pain or swelling to contact a healthcare provider, rest and refrain from exercise, and discontinue CIPRO. Continuing therapy, delaying reporting until rupture, or adding calcium is inconsistent with the label; calcium-containing products can also reduce ciprofloxacin absorption when taken concomitantly.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Section 5.2 directs immediate discontinuation for tendon pain, swelling, inflammation, or rupture. Patient counseling directs contact with the provider, rest and refraining from exercise, and discontinuation. The interaction section states multivalent cation products decrease CIPRO absorption and require separation rather than being used to prevent tendon injury.
